top_categories.workout_context: 160 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Liège-Bastogne-Liège Challenge's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.

Liège-Bastogne-Liège Challenge's paved Ardennes roads with punchy, steep côtes rewards road-specific control. Practice smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 160 miles.
At Liège-Bastogne-Liège Challenge, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
14,764ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
92ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
14,764ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 14,764ft of climbing on paved Ardennes roads with punchy, steep côtes does to your power file on race day.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Liège-Bastogne-Liège Challenge. Train it until it feels boring.
160 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved Ardennes roads with punchy, steep côtes can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Liège-Bastogne-Liège Challenge. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.nutrition: Fueling for 160 miles requires a practiced plan matched to expected duration, intensity, tolerance, and the course's confirmed feed or commercial resupply options. Rehearse the plan on long rides, begin early, carry redundant fuel, and avoid treating a fixed total-calorie estimate as a race prescription.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Liège-Bastogne-Liège Challenge rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on paved ardennes roads with punchy, steep côtes to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Race Simulation, and Road Specific to prepare you for 160 miles of paved ardennes roads with punchy, steep côtes in Banneux, Belgium.
